clf-avc-001.text: A global company must keep its application available even if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable. Which architectural strategy best meets this requirement?
options: Move all data to Amazon S3 Glacier
Deploy the application across multiple Regions with data replication between them
Deploy the application across multiple Availability Zones within one Region
Use only instances Spot to reduce costs
clf-avc-001.explanation: Multiple Availability Zones protect against localized data-center failures, while a multi-Region architecture with appropriate data replication is required to tolerate the loss of an entire Region.

clf-avc-002.text: An organization is reviewing the Performance Efficiency pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework. Which practice is most closely aligned with this pillar?
options: Use the right resource types and technologies for each workload and evolve choices as new technologies become available
Restrict root access and enable MFA for every account
Apply billing tags to every resource
clf-avc-002.explanation: The Performance Efficiency pillar focuses on using computing resources efficiently to meet requirements, selecting appropriate resource types and continuously reviewing technology choices as workloads and AWS capabilities evolve.

clf-avc-003.text: A company adopts a multi-cloud strategy using AWS and another cloud provider at the same time. Which common disadvantage should it consider?
options: Increased operational and management complexity across different platforms
clf-avc-003.explanation: Multi-cloud strategies can increase operational complexity because teams must understand multiple platforms, tools, security models, billing systems, and integration patterns.

clf-avc-004.text: A company with multiple AWS accounts wants centralized security guardrails that prevent member accounts from disabling AWS CloudTrail even if a member-account administrator attempts to do so. Which AWS capability enables this control?
options: IAM policies applied independently in each account
AWS Organizations with Service Control Policies (SCPs)
clf-avc-004.explanation: The Service Control Policies (SCPs) of the AWS Organizations define maximum permissions for member accounts, allowing blocking actions such as disabling CloudTrail throughout the organization.

clf-avc-005.text: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, when a customer uses Amazon RDS as a managed database service, who is responsible for patching the underlying operating system used by the managed database infrastructure?
options: AWS, because Amazon RDS is a managed service
No patching is required for managed services
clf-avc-005.explanation: For managed services such as Amazon RDS, AWS manages more of the underlying infrastructure stack, including operating-system maintenance and patching, while the customer remains responsible for areas such as data, access configuration, and workload-specific settings.

clf-avc-006.text: A company must encrypt data at rest in Amazon S3 and retain granular control over the creation, rotation, access policies, and auditing of the encryption keys. Which option best meets this governance requirement?
options: Client-side encryption only, with no AWS key-management service
Do not encrypt and rely only on IAM controls
SSE-KMS using an AWS KMS customer managed key
SSE-S3 using Amazon S3 managed keys
clf-avc-006.explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer managed AWS KMS key provides granular control over key policies and permissions and supports auditing of key usage through AWS CloudTrail.

clf-avc-007.text: A compliance team must ensure that all Amazon EBS volumes in an account remain encrypted and wants continuous detection when a resource becomes noncompliant. Which AWS service is most appropriate for this continuous configuration evaluation?
clf-avc-007.explanation: AWS Config continuously records and evaluates supported resource configurations against rules, making it suitable for detecting noncompliant resources such as unencrypted EBS volumes.

clf-avc-008.text: A critical transactional database running on an Amazon EC2 instance needs persistent low-latency block storage and point-in-time backup capability through snapshots. Which AWS service should be used?
clf-avc-008.explanation: Amazon EBS provides persistent block storage for EC2 instances, including low-latency volume types suitable for transactional workloads and snapshot support for backup and recovery.

clf-avc-009.text: A company wants to orchestrate Docker containers in production with managed scaling and native AWS integrations while avoiding management of Kubernetes control-plane infrastructure or EC2 worker fleets. Which combination is the most appropriate?
options: AWS Direct Connect with Amazon Route 53
Amazon EC2 without a container orchestrator
clf-avc-009.explanation: Amazon ECS provides AWS-native container orchestration and AWS Fargate provides serverless compute for containers, allowing teams to run container workloads without managing the underlying EC2 server fleet.

clf-avc-010.text: A company must migrate petabytes of data to AWS but has limited internet bandwidth. Which AWS offering is designed for large-scale offline or physical data transfer?
clf-avc-010.explanation: A AWS Snow Family (including Snowball) provides physical devices to transfer large volumes of data to AWS without depending on the bandwidth of the internet.

clf-avc-011.text: A company wants dedicated private network connectivity between its on-premises data center and AWS with more consistent bandwidth and network performance than an internet-based connection. Which AWS service should it use?
clf-avc-011.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides dedicated network connectivity from customer locations to AWS and can deliver more consistent network performance than connections that traverse the public internet.

clf-avc-012.text: A global enterprise wants an AWS Support plan that includes a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), proactive guidance, and the highest level of support for mission-critical workloads. Which support plan provides these capabilities?
clf-avc-012.explanation: AWS Enterprise Support provides designated TAM engagement, proactive guidance, architectural and operational support, and the highest standard support tier for mission-critical workloads.
